result.rationale: The diff changes the Calendar interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` and EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now loops over each destination calendar, calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` per host. But Office365CalendarService.createEvent keeps the old single-argument signature and resolves only `mainHostDestinationCalendar` (`event.destinationCalendar ?? []` first element), ignoring credentialId/which destination it was invoked for — the credential-aware `find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` exists only in GoogleCalendarS

[]` first element), ignoring credentialId/which destination it was invoked for — the credential-aware `find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` exists only in GoogleCalendarService. For collective bookings with multiple destination calendars, every O365 call would target host 1's calendar, causing duplicates or 401/404 errors and missing events on other hosts' calendars. Verifiable mechanism in the diff.

judged_text: Office365CalendarService.createEvent is left on the old single-argument signature and resolves the target as destinationCalendar[0] (mainHostDestinationCalendar), ignoring both the new credentialId parameter and which destination the caller is creating for — the credential-aware find exists only in GoogleCalendarService. For collective bookings with multiple destination calendars, EventManager's per-host loop calls O365 createEvent once per host credential, but every call targets host 1's calendar: host N's event is created in host 1's calendar (duplicate) or fails with 401/404, and host N's own calendar never receives the event.
